'''''Clerodendrum bungei''''', commonly known as '''rose glory bower''', '''glory flower''' or '''Mexican hydrangea''' (though neither a ''[[Hydrangea]]'' nor from Mexico),<ref name=cabi>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cabi.org/isc/datasheet/113370|title=Clerodendrum bungei (rose glorybower)|publisher=Invasive Species Compendium|access-date=20 May 2020}}</ref> is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the deadnettle family, [[Lamiaceae]]. Native to China, it is commonly grown in gardens as an ornamental shrub. It has [[escaped plant|escaped from cultivation]] and is [[naturalisation (biology)|naturalized]] in the Americas.

==Description==
''Clerodendrum bungei'' is a deciduous [[shrub]] that grows up to 2 m in height. Its leaves are [[cordate (leaf shape)|cordate]] (heart-shaped), 10–20 cm long and not quite as wide, and have coarsely toothed edges. The flowers, which appear in late summer, are coloured rose, crimson, or pink, and arranged in a conspicuous rounded [[terminal inflorescence]] known as [[corymb]], which is up to 10 cm in diameter. As in other ''[[Clerodendrum]]'' species, the [[calyx (botany)|calyx]] is five-lobed. At the centre of each flower there is a slender tube {{circa}} 3–4 cm long which terminates in five spreading white lobes. While the flowers are fragrant, crushed leaves have an unpleasant odour.<ref name=Lauener/>

''Clerodendrum bungei'' possess extrafloral [[nectar]]ies that produce a sweet secretion attracting ants (and other arthropods), which in return often protect plant from [[herbivory]].<ref>{{Cite journal | url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2399934 | jstor=2399934 | title=The Genus Clerodendrum (Verbenaceae) in Mesoamerica | last1=Rueda | first1=Ricardo M. | journal=Annals of the Missouri Botanical Garden | year=1993 | volume=80 | issue=4 | pages=870–890 | doi=10.2307/2399934 | url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/268386837_Ant-Plant_Interactions_between_Native_Ants_and_Non-Native_Plants_with_Extrafloral_Nectaries_New_Insights_from_the_Brissago_Islands_Canton_Ticino_Switzerland 
|last1=Marazzi |first1=Brigitte |last2=Bricalli-Rossi-Pedruzzi |first2=Anya and |last3=Forini Giacalone |first3=Isabella |last4=Maspoli |first4=Guido |date= November 2014 |pages=47-56 |title=Ant-Plant Interactions between Native Ants and Non-Native Plants with Extrafloral Nectaries: New Insights from the Brissago Islands (Canton Ticino, Switzerland |volume=102 |journal=Bollettino della Società Ticinese di Scienze Naturali}}</ref>

==Taxonomy==
''Clerodendrum bungei'' was discovered in 1831 by Russian botanist [[Alexander von Bunge (botanist)|Alexander von Bunge]] in [[Beijing]] during his long scientific expedition in [[East Asia]]. Two years later, he [[species description|described]] it as ''C. foetidum'' on the account of the pungent smell of its leaves.<ref name=bunge>{{cite book|author=von Bunge, A.A.|date=1833|page=52|title=Enumeratio Plantarum, quas in China Boreali Collegit}}</ref> Since that name had already been occupied by [[Clerodendrum foetidum|another species]], German botanist [[Ernst Gottlieb von Steudel]] renamed it ''C. bungei'' in 1840.<ref name=Lauener>{{Cite book|first=L. A.|last=Lauener|publisher=SPB Academic Publications|page=50|year=1996|title=The introduction of Chinese plants into Europe}}</ref><ref name=Steud>{{cite journal|author=Steudel, E.G. von|title=Clerodendrum|journal=Nomenclator Botanicus. Editio Secunda|volume= 1|pages=382 |date=1840|url=https://bibdigital.rjb.csic.es/viewer/10859/?offset=#page=386&viewer=picture&o=bookmark&n=0&q=}}</ref> The [[genus]] name is composed of Greek words meaning "chance" and "tree" while the [[specific epithet]] honours Alexander von Bunge.<ref name=missouri/>

==Distribution and habitat==
''Clerodendrum bungei'' is native to Taiwan, Vietnam, and all the mainland [[provinces of China|provinces]] and [[autonomous regions of China]] except [[Jilin]] and [[Liaoning]].<ref name=flora/> It grows along roadsides and in [[mixed forest]]s on mountain slopes below 2500 m.<ref name=flora>{{Cite web|url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=210000300|publisher=Flora of China|title=Clerodendrum bungei|access-date=26 April 2020}}</ref>

==Cultivation==
''Clerodendrum bungei'' was first introduced into Europe {{circa}} 1850 by Scottish plant collector [[Robert Fortune]]. At [[Kew Gardens]] in England it was treated as a [[greenhouse]] plant until another nursery proved its [[winter hardiness]]. As in nature, cultivated plants grow to the height of 2 m. In the [[British Isles]] it is frequently killed to the ground by frost, only to send up "vigorous, erect, woody shoots" the next summer.<ref name=Lauener/> In colder areas, such as the [[U.S. state]] of [[Missouri]], it is grown in containers and overwintered in sunny rooms or [[Conservatory (greenhouse)|conservatories]].<ref name=missouri>{{Cite web|url=http://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=287498|publisher=[[Missouri Botanical Garden]]|title=Clerodendrum bungei|access-date=26 April 2020}}</ref> Its flowers attract butterflies.<ref name=missouri/>

''Clerodendrum bungei'' is noted for its [[suckering]] habit and rapid growth which allow it to form spreading colonies. It is valued for its flowers but its aggressive spread makes it suited best for somewhat isolated areas. ''C. bungei'' has escaped from gardens in [[North America]] and [[Naturalisation (biology)|naturalized]] from [[Texas]] to [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]] and [[Florida]].<ref name=missouri/>
